label: October 5–11
title: “He Hath Borne Our Griefs, and Carried Our Sorrows” —  Isaiah 50

items.text: God sent a deliverer who was not a mighty conqueror, but one who Himself was oppressed and afflicted. Jesus Christ frees us not by opening the prison, but by taking our place there, relieving us from chains of grief and sorrow by bearing them Himself. He suffers with us.

The Lord wanted the Israelites to look to the future with hope, even in captivity. His messages of hope reveal what we can learn about God, and what we can do to make hope a reality in our lives. The future is bright for the Lord’s people.

Isaiah’s prophecies of Christ describe an unexpected deliverer. He was despised and rejected, a man of sorrows acquainted with grief. This unexpected Messiah teaches us about true deliverance, demonstrating God’s ways are not our ways as He saves us from a distance.

Jesus Christ frees us from our chains of grief and sorrow by bearing them Himself. He does not save us from a distance but suffers with us, in acts of ‘everlasting kindness’ that shall not depart from us. His love is personal and enduring.

Few chapters describe Jesus Christ’s redemptive mission more beautifully than Isaiah 53. By pondering what the Savior suffered—the griefs, sorrows, and transgressions He bore for all people and specifically for you, we can feel His love more deeply.

We all have times when we feel distant from the Lord because of our sins or weaknesses. Isaiah 54 and 57 teach that Jesus Christ wants us to return to Him, offering forgiveness and restoration, even when we have given up hope.

God’s ways are not our ways. Where some expected a lion, He sent a lamb. Jesus Christ frees us not by just opening the prison but by taking our place there, relieving us from our chains of grief and sorrow by bearing them Himself.

Helping learners know Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ and feel Their love is paramount. Consider how Israel’s challenges, Isaiah’s prophecies of Christ, and receiving divine help with our own struggles connect to the Savior’s willingness to bear our griefs.

The prophecies in Isaiah 53 are fulfilled in Jesus Christ. He took upon Himself our sins and sorrows, suffering for us. Looking at pictures of His Atonement and pondering His sacrifice can inspire us to act on His teachings.

Isaiah’s message provides hope even during difficult times. By learning about God’s power and His promises of deliverance, we can find strength to face our challenges. We can also learn what actions we can take to make that hope a reality.
